chapter: Recording with King Oliver and Clarence Williams
title: Which King Oliver recording sessions was he on?
summary: Schaap reads out Oliver dates; Waters recalls six sessions mostly at QRS on Long Island and remembers only 'Snag It', insisting the discographies are unreliable.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: PS: You have some very interesting points there. One thing I'd like to grab at immediately is you just mentioned that you made 36 sides with King Oliver. Could you -
36, not sides, 36 - that's 6 sides, 6 sessions. That's 6 sessions, that's about 36 numbers.
PS: Uh huh.
6 sessions.
PS: What were these sessions, there was the one with Clarence Williams in the -
Joe Oliver was there too, sometimes.
PS: Yeah.
Benny Waters 50HP 6/6/82 16
Yeah.
No, well that's -
It was right -
Where are these 6 sessions, did you make the dates he made for Victor in '29?
No.
Or did you make the sessions with him for Decca in the - not Decca, but Vocation in the middle '20's?
Yeah, I'm, here's that - where I made most of them with OKeh. But most of 'em were made in Long Island, QRS.
Uh huh.
'Cause I went there, to Long Island, see. That's where most, the ones that I made.
'Kay, well, let's work backwards. Now give me the date in April of '31 -
Um -
"Careless Love", "One More Time"
No, no -
"When I Take My Sugar To Tea" -
No -
He's probably not on that date, his last solo -
That '31 -
"Sugar Blues", "I'm Crazy 'Bout My Baby" -
No -
for Brunswick, February -
Is that '31? No, I don't remember '31.
Uh -
Benny Waters JOHP 6/6/82
Was it in '27, '28, in that period, same period that Charlie Johnson's band was in?
Yeah, OK, well here, here's a session that was not issued, February 25th of 1928 with Johnny Hodges on the date?
No, I never worked with Johnny, not with him -
Another "Crabhouse Blues", "Who Threw The Rug" - ah, the "Tin Roof Blues" -

I tell you, I tell you, I tell you a record if you got it there, Phil, that I, only one that I remember real well when people have asked me the same story many times. The first thing, I didn't even hear the record, some of 'em, till I got to Europe. That was -
Right -
many years later, see what I mean?
Um hum.
But's one number I remember real well, "Snag It". So whatever sessions that you have "Snag It" on, that's the one I'm on.
OK, well he recorded "Snag It" on March 11th, 1926 in Chicago.
Yeah.
You weren't in Chicago on March 11th, 1926?
No, I'd never been to Chicago then, I was - well he could have done it here, too, in New York, too.
OK, he -
They make it, they make numbers over twice sometimes.
Well, he remade it in Chicago September 17th, 1926. That wouldn't be you either -
No -
would it?
Then in the meantime you can't - Phil, you can't go exactly on those books, they make mistakes, you know.
